policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere נביא and ketiv נביאה are orthographic variants of the same word 'prophet'; ASV 'the prophet' renders either identically and carries no note on this unit, so the base qere fallback stands.

Qere לחטאה and ketiv לחטיא are spelling variants of the same noun 'sin-offering'; ASV 'for a sin-offering' renders either identically and carries no note on this unit, so the base qere fallback stands.
